 COMMON JUDGMENT
These claim petitions are filed under Section 166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
As both petitions were arising out of the same accident, they were clubbed together for recording of common evidence and judgment.

2. The common facts leading to the filing of the top noted petitions are that on 20.12.2023 at about 2.00 p.m, when the  3 SCCH-23  MVC.8683/2023 C/w MVC.8684/2023 petitioner in MVC-8683/2023 being accompanied by two pillion riders (petitioner in MVC-8684/2023 and another by name Shivalinga) was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-E- 1316 near Kamsagara Venkatesh Land, Linganapura,
Kamsagara - Chandahalli road, Mandya, the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MP-0960 came from opposite direction at high speed in a rash & negligent manner and dashed against their motorcycle.
Due to the tremendous impact they fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

After the accident the petitioners were shifted to Government Hospital, Malavalli,
wherein they took first aid and thereafter they were shifted to Venus Multispeciality Hospital, Mysore wherein they took treatment as an inpatient then discharged.

They are still under Siddesh .K.S vs Ramesh on 15 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151605077/
2 treatment and have spent considerable amount towards their medicines, conveyance and other incidental expenses.
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioners have suffered permanent disablement.
The respondent No.1 being the owner of the car and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he was placed exparte.
4. The respondent No.2 filed written statement admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MP-0960.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence,
mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the driver of insured vehicle is denied by this respondent.

Per contra it is alleged that the rider of motorcycle/ petitioner in MVC.8683/2023 who was riding the said vehicle without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
It is further contended that as per the police documents there are three persons including the injured were traveling on a two wheeler, it amounts to violation of section 128 of the MV Act.

In the event of carrying more than one pillion rider on a motorcycle Siddesh .K.S vs Ramesh on 15 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151605077/
3  5 SCCH-23  MVC.8683/2023 C/w MVC.8684/2023 each one of them was contributed negligence in causing the accident.
It is self negligence case as such the claim petition was not maintainable.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured car did not possess valid & effective DL.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a rider.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petitions.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues (which are common in both petitions) were framed:
 ISSUES  1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he  sustained injuries in a road traffic accident  that occurred on 20.12.2023 at about 2.00  p.m., near Kamsagara Venkatesh Land,
 Linganapura, Kamsagara - Chandahalli road,
 Mandya District, due to actionable negligence  of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MP-  0960 ?
 6 SCCH-23  MVC.8683/2023 C/w MVC.8684/2023  2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for  compensation as prayed for ?

If so, at what  rate and from whom ?
 3. What order or award ?

My findings on the above said issues are as under :
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  (in both the petitions)
 Issue No.2  (in both the petitions) : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 :

As per final order  (in both the petitions) for the following:-
 7 SCCH-23  MVC.8683/2023 C/w MVC.8684/2023  REASONS  8. ISSUE NO.1 (IN BOTH THE PETITIONS): The evidence on record reveals that one Shashikumar. K.M lodged the complaint about the occurrence of accident with Halagur police.
After receipt of the complaint the said police registered an FIR against the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MP-0960 and took up investigation.
During the course of investigation material evidence connected to the accident was collected by them.
The Wound certificates marked at Ex's.P5 and 14 disclose that the petitioners sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
A close look at the spot mahazar indicates that accident has occurred in the manner as alleged by the petitioners.
Even the damages caused to both the vehicles as per IMV report supports this aspect.

Be that as it may, the IMV Siddesh .K.S vs Ramesh on 15 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151605077/
5 inspector has mentioned that he tested both the vehicles and found that their brake systems were in order.
He has thereby opined that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the said vehicles.
Therefore the driver of the car did not have sufficient cause to have lost control of his vehicle.

Such being  8 SCCH-23  MVC.8683/2023 C/w MVC.8684/2023 the case, the very fact that he dashed against the motorcycle on which the petitioners were proceeding leads to drawing of an inference that he was driving his vehicle rashly & negligently.

Hence the jurisdictional police have also filed charge sheet against him for the offences punishable under section's 279,
337 & 338 of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

9. During the course of cross-examination of PW's.1 & 2,
the learned counsel for insurance company could not elicit anything worthwhile to negate their testimonies.
Apart from that perusal of the written statement filed by the respondent No.2 shows that the insurance company has taken divergent stands.
At one stretch it has denied the very involvement of its insured vehicle and at another it has contended that there was no negligence on the part of driver of its insured vehicle.

Thus,
absolutely there is no merit in the defence taken by respondent No.2.

The main contention of the insurance company is that the petitioner in MVC.8683/2023 (PW.1) who was riding his motorcycle with two persons on the pillion, has contributed his  9 SCCH-23  MVC.8683/2023 C/w MVC.8684/2023 Siddesh .K.S vs Ramesh on 15 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151605077/
6 negligence in the occurrence of the accident.
However the fact that PW.1 was riding a motorcycle accompanied by two pillion riders, may not, by itself, without anything more, make him guilty of contributory negligence.
At the most, he would be guilty of being a party to the violation of law.

But such violation by itself, without anything more, cannot lead to a finding of contributory negligence unless it is established that it is the very act of PW.1 riding along with two others contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon him and the other petitioners.
10 . In this regard the respondnet No.2 relied the decision reported in 2003 0 Supreme (AP) 1460, in case of United India Insurance Company Limited v/s K. Anjaiah.

sentences.text: As held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Mohammed Siddique and another V/s National Insurance Co.Ltd and Others 'There must either be causal connection between the violation and the accident or a causal connection between the violation and the impact of the accident upon the victim.

sentences.text: It is in such cases, where, but for the violation of Law, either the accident could have been averted or the impact could have been minimized, that the principle of contributory negligence could be invoked'.
In the instant petition it is not the defence of the insurer that the accident would have been averted, if three persons were not riding on the motorcycle.
Nothing worthwhile was either extracted from PW.1's mouth to the effect that two persons on the pillion added to the imbalance.

Therefore, in the absence of any evidence to show that the wrongful act on the part of PW.1 contributed either to the accident or to the nature Siddesh .K.S vs Ramesh on 15 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151605077/
8 of injuries sustained, he cannot be held guilty of contributory negligence.

sentences.text: Further to prove contributory negligence there must be cogent evidence.

In the case on hand there is no specific evidence to establish that the accident took place due to rash &
 12 SCCH-23  MVC.8683/2023 C/w MVC.8684/2023 negligent act of PW.1.
In the absence of same, the Doctrine of Common Law cannot be applied in the present case.
14. Interestingly the respondent No.2 which denied the very involvement of its insured car as well as the manner of occurrence of the accident has not led any evidence to this effect.
Further the insurance company did not make any attempt to examine the driver of its insured car who is the best witness to depose about the cause of accident.
There is no explanation to that effect.
Non-examination of the said driver is fatal to the defence of respondent No.2.
Hence its contention that there was no negligence on the part of driver of car has to be disbelieved.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW's.1 & 2 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to negligence of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MP-0960.

With this observation issue No.1 (in both the petitions) is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.

It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA. No.101144/2020 (MV) dated. 05.07.2023.

Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
 "(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The  Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased  at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of  Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.

To substantiate the  14 SCCH-23  MVC.8683/2023 C/w MVC.8684/2023  said claim, the injured claimant has not placed  any material on record, it is for the Courts and  Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The  notional income fixed by the Karnataka State  Legal Services Authority for the accident of the  year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any  material produced by the claimant to prove his  income, it is appropriate to assess the notional  income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per  month, and the same is assessed as the monthly  income of the injured claimant"
As such this Court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.

Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on Siddesh .K.S vs Ramesh on 15 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151605077/

Therefore he got examined Dr.S. Ramachandra as PW.3, who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has sustained total permanent physical disability of 34.50% of right lower limb and 17.25%

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant  16 SCCH-23  MVC.8683/2023 C/w MVC.8684/2023 for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 6%, cannot be ruled out.

Therefore, I consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 6%.

opennyai_summary.facts:
These claim petitions are filed under Section 166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
As both petitions were arising out of the same accident, they were clubbed together for recording of common evidence and judgment.
Due to the tremendous impact they fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
After the accident the petitioners were shifted to Government Hospital, Malavalli,
wherein they took first aid and thereafter they were shifted to Venus Multispeciality Hospital, Mysore wherein they took treatment as an inpatient then discharged.
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioners have suffered permanent disablement.
The respondent No.1 being the owner of the car and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he was placed exparte.
4. The respondent No.2 filed written statement admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MP-0960.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner proves that he  sustained injuries in a road traffic accident  that occurred on 20.12.2023 at about 2.00  p.m., near Kamsagara Venkatesh Land,
 Linganapura, Kamsagara - Chandahalli road,
 Mandya District, due to actionable negligence  of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MP-  0960 ?
 6 SCCH-23  MVC.8683/2023 C/w MVC.8684/2023  2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for  compensation as prayed for ?
If so, at what  rate and from whom ?
 3. What order or award ?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Therefore the driver of the car did not have sufficient cause to have lost control of his vehicle.
However the fact that PW.1 was riding a motorcycle accompanied by two pillion riders, may not, by itself, without anything more, make him guilty of contributory negligence.
At the most, he would be guilty of being a party to the violation of law.
But such violation by itself, without anything more, cannot lead to a finding of contributory negligence unless it is established that it is the very act of PW.1 riding along with two others contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon him and the other petitioners.
Further the respondent No.2 contended that as the petition is not maintainable as the death of or personal injury caused to Workmen in Motor accident arising out of and in court of employment and relied on the decision reported in (2005) 6 SCC 172 in the case of National Insurance Co.Ltd., V/s Premabai Patel and others.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Such being  8 SCCH-23  MVC.8683/2023 C/w MVC.8684/2023 the case, the very fact that he dashed against the motorcycle on which the petitioners were proceeding leads to drawing of an inference that he was driving his vehicle rashly & negligently.
Hence the jurisdictional police have also filed charge sheet against him for the offences punishable under section's 279,
337 & 338 of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
As held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Mohammed Siddique and another V/s National Insurance Co.Ltd and Others 'There must either be causal connection between the violation and the accident or a causal connection between the violation and the impact of the accident upon the victim.
It is in such cases, where, but for the violation of Law, either the accident could have been averted or the impact could have been minimized, that the principle of contributory negligence could be invoked'.
In the instant petition it is not the defence of the insurer that the accident would have been averted, if three persons were not riding on the motorcycle.
Nothing worthwhile was either extracted from PW.1's mouth to the effect that two persons on the pillion added to the imbalance.
Therefore, in the absence of any evidence to show that the wrongful act on the part of PW.1 contributed either to the accident or to the nature Siddesh .K.S vs Ramesh on 15 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151605077/
8 of injuries sustained, he cannot be held guilty of contributory negligence.
Further to prove contributory negligence there must be cogent evidence.
In the case on hand there is no specific evidence to establish that the accident took place due to rash &
 12 SCCH-23  MVC.8683/2023 C/w MVC.8684/2023 negligent act of PW.1.
In the absence of same, the Doctrine of Common Law cannot be applied in the present case.
14. Interestingly the respondent No.2 which denied the very involvement of its insured car as well as the manner of occurrence of the accident has not led any evidence to this effect.
It is needless to say that the said injury is grievous in nature.
It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to accidental injuries he has become disabled and lost his earning capacity.
Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant  16 SCCH-23  MVC.8683/2023 C/w MVC.8684/2023 for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
